claim: A multi-line string whose content ends with a quote character (TOML closes it with 4 or 5 quotes, e.g. a = ["""x""""]) is closed at the first three quotes; the extra quote starts a basic string that swallows the following ']' so depth stays 1. Same for ''' literal strings.
what_goes_wrong: A multi-line string ending in a quote (valid TOML, e.g. a = ["""x""""]) leaves depth at 1, so lean_config treats following lines as inside an array and a later top-level `notify = ...` key is not dropped from the worker's config.
fix_idea: After finding the closing delimiter, extend it over any additional run of the same quote character (up to 2 more) before resuming the scan.

claim: In --changed mode, a function whose last body lines were deleted is missed when git reports the deletion as a mixed hunk (old lines removed and a new line added right after the function, e.g. a comment replacing the blank line). hunk_ranges records no deleted_ranges for a mixed hunk and the new line lies outside the function, so the changed function is not a target.
what_goes_wrong: When a commit removes the last lines of a function and adds a line just outside it (a mixed hunk), `hpflow targets --changed A..B` leaves out the changed function, so it is never reviewed.
fix_idea: In hunk_ranges, add the old range to deleted_ranges whenever old_count > 0, not only when new_count is 0. Then the old function's overlap with it marks the new function as changed.

claim: The per-file `git diff` gets the file name as a pathspec, so glob characters in a name (e.g. `a*.py`) are expanded. The diff of that file then also includes other files that match (`ab.py`), and their hunks are added to its ranges.
what_goes_wrong: A changed file whose name has glob characters (*, ?, [) gets the hunks of other files that match its name as a pathspec, so `hpflow targets --changed` picks functions that did not change in that file.
fix_idea: Pass the file names as literal pathspecs, e.g. prefix each with `:(literal)` or run git with `--literal-pathspecs`, in the per-file diff and the first diff.

claim: hunk_ranges splits the diff with str.splitlines(), which also breaks at form feed, \x1c-\x1e, \x85 and \u2028/\u2029. A changed line that holds such a character followed by text like '@@ -50 +50 @@' is read as a hunk header, so a fake range is added.
what_goes_wrong: A changed source line containing a form feed, \x1c-\x1e, \x85 or \u2028/\u2029 followed by text like '@@ -50 +50 @@' is split into its own line by splitlines() and read as a hunk header, adding a fake range so unrelated functions are reported as changed.
fix_idea: Split only on '\n' (diff.split('\n')) so content characters cannot create new lines.

claim: check() runs at most 12 related test files (related[:12]) and silently drops the rest without reporting them, so a failing related test beyond the first 12 is never run and the change is accepted although the docstring requires that the tests naming the changed module must pass.
what_goes_wrong: When more than 12 repository tests name the changed module, the extras are dropped without a word, so a fix that breaks one of them is accepted although the contract says the related tests must pass.
fix_idea: Run all related tests (or in batches), or report the dropped ones in the result like large_test_files_not_run, and reject or flag when some were not run.
